newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open 0.66 pct higher ahead of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open 0.66 pct higher ahead of FOMC.

text.p: French shares opened higher on Tuesday on the back of a sharp turnaround on Wall Street ahead of a Federal Reserve Open Market Committee meeting starting at 1400 GMT.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 24.94 points or 0.97 percent at 2,604.22 at 0903 GMT after having opened 0.66 percent higher at 2,596.33.
The CAC-40 futures contract rose to 2,606 from 2,580 on Monday's close.
The market is expecting a 0.25 percentage point increase in Fed funds rates today, dealers said.

Lyonnaise des Eaux and Cie de Suez remained strong on the back of an expected share swap bid of two Suez shares for one Lyonnaise share as part of a friendly merger. Lyonnaise was up 0.87 percent at 579 and Suez added 0.79 percent to 279.50 francs.

Daily Liberation said on Monday that Lyonnaise may also seek a deal with Bouygues in audiovisual activities. Bouygues is main stakeholder in TF1 and Lyonnaise has cable activities, a stake in M6 and the TPS digital satellite venture.
French media had speculated last week about a telecommunications link between Bouygues and Lyonnaise.
Lyonnaise des Eaux said on Friday that it would choose an ally in the telecommunications sector before the summer. It and Bouygues had no comment on a report in Le Monde about a telecoms tie-up.

Bouygues, up 1.8 percent at 564 francs, is the main shareholder in Bouygues Telecom, with Decaux and Italy's STET. It runs France's third mobile telecoms network and plans to rival France Telecom and Generale des Eaux unit Cegetel in wider telecoms operations in 1998.
Le Figaro on Tuesday also suggested Bouygues Telecom could be floated to raise money for expansion.
Textile group Damart was the biggest riser with a 9.98 percent gain on the back of a leap in first half profits to 147.6 million francs from 47.4 million.
